_README: Hand-built evaluation set. Every judged paper id was verified present in the corpus
(scripts/evaluate.py --validate re-checks this) and resolved from arXiv itself rather
Grades: 3 = this IS the paper asked for, 2 = highly relevant, 1 = marginally relevant.
This file is TEST data. It must never be used to train the ranker - the training pairs
come from mined citation contexts instead. Overlap would invalidate every reported number.
Intents are scored separately because they fail differently: text-only retrieval is
weakest on specific_paper queries, and an aggregate average hides that.

Queries prefixed 'obscure-' are ADVERSARIAL: their correct answers sit in the 55th-96th citation percentile rather than the 99.9th, so a ranker that simply sorts by citation count cannot solve them. They exist because the original set was built from landmark papers and therefore could not detect popularity collapse.
